**Search run:** EBI Job Dispatcher `ncbiblast`, **blastx** of the first 1400 nt against **UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot** (575,748 sequences; BLASTX 2.16.0+). EBI job `ncbiblast-R20261104-075508-0318-56765991-p2m`, process `a15e6596-b031-4f2b-b2c0-fadd4a23f2d5`. I chose blastx against Swiss-Prot because it is taxonomically unbiased and returns in seconds, whereas a nucleotide search of all of ENA takes ~45–70 min.

**Top hits — four different genes, all full-length 100% identity to phiX174:**

| Hit | Protein | Identity | E-value |
|---|---|---|---|
| P69486 `SCAFD_BPPHS` | External scaffolding protein D, phage phiX174 (Isolate Sanger) | 152/152 (100%) | 4e-100 |
| P03641 `CAPSD_BPPHS` | Capsid protein F, phage phiX174 | 133/133 (100%) | 9e-87 |
| P69172 `C_BPPHS` | Protein C, phage phiX174 | 86/86 (100%) | 2e-52 |
| P69594 `K_BPPHS` | Protein K, phage phiX174 | 56/56 (100%) | 9e-28 |
| P03639 `LYS_BPPHS` | Lysis protein E, phage phiX174 | 90/91 (99%) | 2e-55 |

**Discriminating it from its close relatives:** the Microviridae relatives all appear in the hit list, and the capsid protein F separates them cleanly — 133/133 (100%) to phiX174 P03641 versus 130/133 (98%) to phage S13 P07931, and only 72–73% to G4 (P03642), phiK (Q38041) and alpha3 (P08767). Protein D is identical in phiX174 and S13 (hence the tied 4e-100 for P69487/P69486), so F is what settles it. The call is phiX174, not S13.

**Note on the name:** this is a bacteriophage, not a bacterium. "Escherichia phage" in the header refers to its *host* (*E. coli*) — the sequence itself is the virus genome, not *E. coli* DNA.

**Still running:** I also submitted the definitive nucleotide-level search — blastn vs `em_all` (all of ENA = GenBank equivalent) — as background process **`6126b8d2-54c7-4a41-b947-911dedc4d90b`**. It takes 45–70 min and will land in `blast-results/` in the workspace. The protein evidence above is already conclusive, so that job is corroboration (it should return NC_001422.1 / J02482 at ~100% nucleotide identity); ask me and I'll check its status.

Confidence: very high — this is an alignment lookup, not a prediction. Five independent gene-level hits at 100%/99% identity with E-values from 4e-100 to 9e-28.
